saw_lines: People selling a car want a number fast, and they compare two or three offers before they hand over keys.
So the sale is won in line one, where a price or cash promise answers the question before they call a rival.
Your site shows prices from $1 to $750, yet 0 of 30 ads mention price. Lead one ad with the price so buyers see the number first.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 25 Nov 2026
points: Your site shows prices from $1 to $750, yet 0 of 30 ads mention price, so a seller weighing offers has nothing to compare. Open one ad with a price from your site, and test it against the cash promise ad.
No proof number in your ads
None of your 30 ads shows a proof number, so a seller has no reason to trust a stranger with a car. Pull one real figure, a review count or cars bought, and lead three new ads with it.
0 of 18 ads carry an offer, so new buyers have no reason to act today. Give them one reason, such as a first order offer or a bundle, and put it in line one of three new ads.

23 ads have run 60 days or more, yet none of your 7 newer ads reuses a winner’s opening line, so the proven hook goes unused. Build the next three ads as variations of your oldest winner, changing only the second line.
